lead.headline: Oil Hits a Six-Month High as Riyadh Airport Partly Reopens
lead.deck: Brent closes at $116.72 while the Houthis keep firing at the kingdom.
body: The world's main oil price, Brent crude, closed at $116.72 a barrel on Friday. That was up 3.1% on the day and its highest close since 29 April, and Brent rose 6.2% over the week, its third weekly gain in a row. US crude, known as WTI, settled at $103.27.

Three worries pushed the price up. The Houthis, an armed group from Yemen, Saudi Arabia's southern neighbour, keep attacking the kingdom. There was also a reported oil spill off the United Arab Emirates. And traders were betting on renewed US strikes on Iran: US officials told The New York Times that the US and Israel have plans for fresh strikes after the 3 November midterm elections.

Those attacks have reached the capital. Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport had been shut for about two weeks after strikes earlier in October. On Sunday, Terminal 1 reopened for domestic flights and Terminal 2 for international ones. The same day, the Saudi-led coalition said it shot down a ballistic missile and a drone aimed at Riyadh, and ten ballistic missiles aimed at the south.

The Houthis' spokesman called the airport unsafe and a “military target”. Airlines are cautious: Emirates says its flights to Riyadh and Dammam will resume on 8 November. Meanwhile, the US has ordered staff not needed for emergencies out of Saudi Arabia, and American embassies in the region have tightened security as warnings of Iranian plots grow. Saudi Arabia is one of the world's biggest oil exporters, which is why every attack on it is felt at petrol pumps far away.

world.headline: Serbia's Students Take Their Protest to the Ballot Box
world.deck: A snap election tests the longtime leader Aleksandar Vucic.
body: In 2024, a canopy at a newly renovated railway station in the city of Novi Sad collapsed and killed 16 people. Students then led protests that lasted almost two years, against alleged corruption, the misuse of power for private gain, and authoritarianism, meaning rule that ignores limits on power.

On Sunday those protests reached the ballot box. Serbia held a snap election, one called early, for all 250 seats in its parliament. The whole country votes as a single constituency, so seats are shared out according to each list's share of the national vote. The students backed a list of 250 candidates, many of them academics or political outsiders, led by cardiologist Ilija Srdanovic and running against corruption.

Their opponent is Aleksandar Vucic, Serbia's longtime leader. He resigned as president in September to run for prime minister. Reuters called the vote the biggest challenge to his rule for more than a decade. An Ipsos poll gave his SNS party 47% and the students 40%, but other polls put the students ahead, and Serbia lacks reliable independent polling. One analyst expected a “very tight” result.

Early turnout was strong, with long lines at polling stations. Opponents of Vucic and some independent monitoring groups warned of possible irregularities in the voting. Vucic, for his part, warned that any protests claiming fraud if his party won would be quickly put down.

A list needs at least 3% of the vote to win seats, so small parties can be shut out. Polls closed at 8pm local time, with first indications of the result expected about two hours later. The official count is not expected before Monday.

world.connect: Serbia's students are not the first young people to challenge a government. From civil rights marches in the US to Gen-Z protests in Asia, young people have often pushed for change, but elections are where protests are tested.

india.headline: Cyclone Arnab Heads for the Andhra Pradesh Coast
india.deck: Odisha shuts schools in five districts as two states brace for the storm.
body: A cyclone is a giant spinning storm that feeds on warm sea water, like a vast whirlpool of wind. A depression, an area of low pressure, over the Bay of Bengal is expected to turn into Cyclone Arnab and head for India's east coast.

The India Meteorological Department expects it to cross the coast between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam, in Andhra Pradesh, by the forenoon of 28 October as a “very severe cyclonic storm”. Winds could average 115 to 125 km an hour, with gusts of 140. Heavy to very heavy rain is forecast for coastal Andhra Pradesh from 27 to 29 October.

Southern Odisha, just to the north, is under a red alert. Schools, colleges and Anganwadi centres in Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput and Malkangiri will close on 28 and 29 October. Around 60 state rescue teams, 17 National Disaster Response Force teams and 225 fire service teams are on alert.
india.why: Warnings issued days ahead, shelters and teams in place before the wind arrives are how India's coasts have learned to live with cyclones.
also: Markets: The Sensex fell for a fourth straight day on Friday, to 73,123.83, as oil passed $114 a barrel.
Andhra Pradesh: Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu told officials to be on high alert; 25,000 electric poles are ready.

us.headline: The US Birth Rate Falls to Its Lowest Level Ever Recorded
us.deck: Fewer babies were born in 2025, but older mothers softened the fall.
body: Every year the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention counts the babies born in the US. Its new report says the general fertility rate, the number of births for every 1,000 women of childbearing age, fell 1% in 2025 to its lowest level ever recorded. About 3.6 million babies were born, at a rate of roughly 53 per 1,000 women.
The drop was steepest for younger women. The rate fell 6% for women aged 20 to 24 and about 7% for teenagers. It rose a little for women aged 30 to 45, which kept the overall fall small.

The 2025 rate is nearly 20% below the rate two decades ago. A Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta study found that women in Generation Z are much less likely to want children than earlier generations. Researchers also point to people marrying and starting families later, and some experts argue that more women would have children if housing and childcare cost less.

us.why: Births today decide how many students, workers and taxpayers a country will have in 20 years, which shapes schools, jobs and care for older people.

sports.title: BASEBALL: BREWERS RALLY FOR A 2-0 SERIES LEAD
sports.body: The Milwaukee Brewers came back from 4-0 down to beat the Tampa Bay Rays 5-4 in Game 2 of the World Series. Sal Frelick tied it with a sixth-inning home run, and Cooper Pratt's single in the seventh brought in the winning run. Milwaukee needs two more wins; Game 3 is on Monday.

body: Serbia is a country in Europe. In 2024 a roof at a train station fell down, and 16 people died. Many people blamed corruption, which means leaders being dishonest.
Students protested for almost two years. On Sunday, Serbia held an early election for its parliament of 250 seats. The students backed their own list of candidates.

us.headline: Fewer Babies Are Born in America
body: The birth rate counts how many babies are born for every 1,000 women. In 2025 the US rate fell to its lowest level ever recorded.
About 3.6 million babies were born. The rate fell most for women in their early twenties and for teenagers.
